decisions.thought: Ribombee is frail (base 60 HP) and weak to Ghost/Steel. Gholdengo's Make It Rain (Steel, 120 BP) is super-effective and likely OHKOs even without Tera. Tera Steel would boost the damage further but isn't necessary for the KO. Shadow Ball is also super-effective but lower power. Focus Blast is weaker accuracy and not needed. Nasty Plot wastes the turn. No switch is needed since we can secure a quick KO. Best play: Make It Rain for maximum damage and guaranteed OHKO.

Ribombee is faster and has Focus Sash. Setting Sticky Web is the ideal lead move: it will survive any hit and set up a crucial speed hazard. Even though Gholdengo has Air Balloon, the web is on the field and will punish grounded switch-ins later. No other move is as impactful this turn.

Ribombee is at 1.0% HP — effectively a guaranteed KO. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball (Ghost) is super-effective against Bug/Fairy and will secure the knockout. No need to waste Tera or a stronger move. The opponent's Ribombee revealed Sticky Web, but our Gholdengo is already active and faster (SPE 293 vs Ribombee's 124). Eliminating Ribombee removes the Sticky Web setter and gives us a clean board for the next turn. Shadow Ball is the most efficient choice — high accuracy, super-effective, and sufficient damage to finish a 1% HP target.

Ribombee is at 1 HP and outspends Gholdengo. Sticky Web is already set, so further field entry isn't needed. Moonblast is resisted by Steel/Ghost, Stun Spore is unreliable and leaves us prone. U-turn lets us hit first, then safely bring in a better attacker (Iron Valiant) that can threaten with Ghost coverage. Direct switching would let Gholdengo attack our new switch-in for free. U-turn minimizes risk and maintains momentum.

Ribombee is at 1 HP and cannot stay in. Gholdengo is slower and likely has -1 SpA from Make It Rain. Iron Valiant outspeeds it and threatens with a super-effective Shadow Ball after switching in. It also has high special attack and can apply immediate pressure. Other options are slower or lack an effective hit on Gholdengo. Switching to Iron Valiant is the best tactical move.

Iron Valiant is at 47% and has -1 Special Defense, so it's a prime target. Gholdengo resists Fairy and is immune to Fighting; Moonblast is poor, and Close Combat is immune. Shadow Ball is only neutral STAB-less damage. Meanwhile, opponent Gholdengo is Ghost/Steel, so Kingambit resists both Shadow Ball and Make It Rain very well (Ghost 4x resist, Steel 2x resist) and has full HP. It can pivot in, take a weak hit, and threaten with Kowtow Cleave. Sticky Web slows the opponent, so Kingambit's decent Speed is sufficient. This is the best defensive and offensive pivot.

Iron Valiant at 48% HP with SpD at -1. Make It Rain (Steel) is super effective against Fairy (2x). Gholdengo's SPA is -1 but damage should still secure the KO. Gholdengo outspeeds (293 vs 116 base SPE). No need for Tera since Steel STAB is already active. Shadow Ball is neutral, Focus Blast is resisted by Fairy.

Opponent Kingambit at 77% HP. Gholdengo has -2 SPA, making Make It Rain (Steel) weak. Focus Blast (Fighting) is neutral and hits harder despite lower accuracy. With Good as Gold, status moves are blocked, so Nasty Plot won't work. Shadow Ball is resisted. Focus Blast has ~70% accuracy but can KO or heavily damage Kingambit. Tera Fighting would boost Focus Blast's power and accuracy, making it the strongest option. No speed control or priority threats visible. Tera Focus Blast is the best KO attempt.

Opponent is Gholdengo with -2 SpA and likely low speed due to sticky web. We are faster and carry dark-type STAB super effective vs Ghost. Kowtow Cleave is guaranteed to hit and will KO; Sucker Punch risks failing if they status. No need to Tera or switch. Use Kowtow Cleave to eliminate it and maintain damage on our side.

Opponent Kingambit at 77% HP. My Gholdengo is Terastallized Fighting with -2 SPA. Focusblast (Fighting) is STAB and super-effective against Dark/Steel. Even with -2 SPA, Focusblast should deal significant damage. Kingambit's low Sp. Def (85 base) makes it vulnerable. Focusblast has 70% accuracy but the potential to KO or severely damage is high. Make It Rain is Steel-type, neutral damage, and Shadow Ball is Ghost, neutral. Nasty Plot would boost SPA but wastes a turn. The decisive factor is securing a KO or major damage on the opponent's active threat. Focusblast is the best option despite accuracy concerns.
